_metadata.independence: Apart from the brief, I read only x16-rc-input.json and no other repository, scratchpad or web source.

hints.reason: ANGEL via the archangel Raphael, NINJA via the red-masked Ninja Turtle Raphael; two famous Raphaels give a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Strong two-reference double meaning; both sides accurate.

hints.reason: ASTRONAUT via Buzz Aldrin (with Buzz Lightyear as a bonus echo), BEE via the buzzing sound; clean and instantly satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Classic clean double meaning.

hints.reason: BAR via the musical measure (US musicians say measure for bar), RULER via a ruler being a measuring tool; fair and tidy.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; the music sense of BAR gives a small aha.

hints.reason: BASEBALL via the pitch the pitcher throws, FIELD via pitch as a sports field (soccer pitch is familiar to US players too).
hints.fix: In baseball, the pitcher starts each at-bat by throwing a pitch.

pairs.pair_note: Good double meaning; the soccer-pitch sense is well known in the US. The BASEBALL line overstates slightly (not every play, e.g. a pickoff, starts with a pitch); optional softening offered.

hints.reason: BED via the pile of mattresses the pea sits under, PRINCESS via The Princess and the Pea; tiny word, big recognition.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent fairy-tale link; both lines accurate.

hints.reason: BILL via Bill Nye the Science Guy, NEW YEAR via NYE as the standard shorthand for New Year's Eve; a sly, satisfying click.

pairs.pair_note: Clever. Only doubt (hence uncertain): NYE is essentially an abbreviation of a phrase built on the target NEW YEAR, which some might see as encoding the target; I judge it fair because the hint is a real name and does not contain the target word.

hints.reason: BOMB and BUS both via the film Speed, whose bus bomb explodes if the bus drops below 50 mph; iconic premise.

pairs.pair_note: Strong film link; explanation accurate (the trigger is falling below 50 mph).

hints.reason: BOW via Cupid's bow and arrows, VALENTINE via Cupid as the Valentine's Day icon; easy but clean.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, fair, accurate.

hints.reason: BROWN via UPS's famous brown trucks and uniforms ('What can Brown do for you?'), DELIVERY via UPS delivering packages.

pairs.pair_note: Brand link most US players get at once.

hints.reason: BUTTON via belly button = navel, ORANGE via the navel orange; a genuine oh-nice double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; both lines accurate.

hints.reason: SUPERHERO via Marvel's Daredevil is instant, but CANNON only via the generic idea that a human-cannonball performer is a daredevil, which many players would not reach from the hint.

pairs.pair_note: Superhero side is strong; cannon side is a loose stunt association. No clearly better one-word hint found (CANNONBALL, also a Marvel hero, contains the target).

hints.reason: CAST via the familiar cast-iron skillet, PAN via skillet being a frying pan; honest and easy.

pairs.pair_note: Fine phrase-join plus synonym; the cast-iron skillet is instantly familiar.

hints.reason: CHANGE via shift meaning a change, KEYBOARD via the Shift key; clean double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Solid and fair.

hints.reason: CHEST via 'chest of drawers', DRESSER via a dresser being furniture full of drawers; true and easy, if flat.

pairs.pair_note: Honest but low delight since a dresser is essentially a chest of drawers; still a fair clue.

hints.reason: CINDERELLA via her magic ending at midnight, STRIKE via the clock striking midnight; the famous scene ties both.

pairs.pair_note: Lovely; STRIKE in its clock sense gives a nice aha.

hints.reason: COAT via a fleece jacket and a sheep's coat of fleece, RAM via a ram's fleece (and the Golden Fleece came from a ram).

pairs.pair_note: Good; accurate.

hints.reason: COTTON via 'cotton swab', EAR via swabs used on the outer ear; instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and easy; the EAR line responsibly says outer ear.

hints.reason: COWBOY via roping cattle with a lasso, SUPERHERO via Wonder Woman's Lasso of Truth; nice cross-genre aha.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: DANCE via the famous Thriller dance, ZOMBIE via the zombies who rise and dance in the video.

pairs.pair_note: Iconic and accurate.

hints.reason: DESSERT via the layered trifle dessert, SMALL via 'a trifle' meaning something small or unimportant.

pairs.pair_note: Clever double meaning; trifle the dessert is known in the US.

hints.reason: DOCTOR via a quack being a fake doctor, DUCK via the duck's quack; classic aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: DOWN via crossword clues running across and down, PUZZLE via 'crossword puzzle'; fair and familiar.

pairs.pair_note: The DOWN side gives a small aha; fine.

hints.reason: EARTH via a globe as a model of Earth, THEATER via Shakespeare's Globe Theatre; satisfying once THEATER clicks.

pairs.pair_note: Good; the Globe Theatre is widely taught in US schools.

hints.reason: FRANCE via Emperor Napoleon, FARM via Napoleon the pig in Orwell's Animal Farm; strong literary aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent and accurate.

hints.reason: FLASH via camera flashes, HOLLYWOOD via photographers chasing Hollywood stars; easy, pleasant scene.

pairs.pair_note: Fair scene clue.

hints.reason: GAME via the board game Battleship, SINK via sinking ships ('You sank my battleship!'); easy but fun.

pairs.pair_note: GAME side is broad but the famous catchphrase makes it land.

hints.reason: GLOVE via a baseball mitt, OVEN via an oven mitt; clean and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Good; mitt being a kind of glove is not a problem.

hints.reason: HAMMER via a gavel being a small wooden hammer, JUDGE via the judge's gavel; easy and accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, fair.

hints.reason: HERO via the mythic hero Hercules, STRENGTH via Hercules as a byword for strength; easy and true.
hints.fix: Hercules (Heracles to the Greeks) is the mythic hero famous for his strength.

pairs.pair_note: Fine clue. Pedantic note: Hercules is the Roman name for the Greek Heracles; optional wording fix offered.

hints.reason: INSECT via bug as insect, SPY via a bug as a hidden listening device; classic double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; matches the owner's approved BUG pattern.

hints.reason: KNIFE and SHOWER both via the famous Psycho shower scene; instantly recognisable film link.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; reference is iconic and not graphic in the text.

hints.reason: LION via Aslan, WINTER via the White Witch's endless winter; both central to The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe.

pairs.pair_note: Strong. ASLAN would only cover LION, so NARNIA is the right pick.

hints.reason: MEXICO via Maya sites such as Chichen Itza, PYRAMID via Maya step pyramids; true and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Fair; AZTEC is a comparable alternative but not clearly better.

hints.reason: NETFLIX via binge-watching culture, SEASON via bingeing a whole season; familiar modern link.
hints.fix: Netflix often drops whole seasons at once for bingeing.

pairs.pair_note: Good clue; the NETFLIX line overstates (some Netflix shows release in parts or weekly), so 'often' is suggested.

hints.reason: OLD via vintage meaning old and classic, WINE via a wine's vintage year; clean double meaning.
hints.fix: A wine's vintage is the year its grapes were harvested.

pairs.pair_note: Good; the WINE line should match the explanation (harvest year, not simply the year it was made).

hints.reason: PEPPER via Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band, YELLOW via Yellow Submarine; two iconic titles, instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Title phrase-join, but both titles are iconic (and Sgt. Pepper's band even appears in the Yellow Submarine film); passes the instantly-familiar bar.

hints.reason: PIPE via Popeye's corncob pipe, SAIL via 'Popeye the Sailor Man'; classic cartoon recall.

pairs.pair_note: Strong classic reference.

hints.reason: POISON via venom as a bite-delivered poison, SPIDER via spider venom and Spider-Man's foe Venom; good double route.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; synonym on the POISON side is fine because SPIDER has two routes.

hints.reason: QUEEN via Queen Victoria is instant, but SPONGE needs the Victoria sponge cake, a British bake many US players (outside Bake Off fans) won't know.

pairs.pair_note: Facts are true (cake named for Queen Victoria; jam-and-cream filling is a common version). Verdict hinges on US familiarity with the Victoria sponge, so a second opinion is worthwhile.

hints.reason: ROPE via her hair let down like a rope, TOWER via the tower she is locked in; iconic.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent fairy-tale link.

hints.reason: SOLDIER via the toy-soldier nutcracker, SUGAR via the Sugar Plum Fairy; satisfying ballet link.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; SUGAR via the Sugar Plum Fairy is a nice aha.

hints.reason: WOOD via the wooden puppet, STRING via 'I've Got No Strings' and puppet strings; strong Disney recall.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent and accurate.
